values.note: No fee. OHV Special Recreation Permits apply only to riders on the OHV trails.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/little-fort-campground ('Fee Site and Info: No Fee'; 'OHV Special Recreation Permits apply to users of OHV/ATV Trail'; page last updated 2025-12-11), read 2026-10-20

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/little-fort-campground ('Seasons of Use: Open year round'; status 'Site Open'), read 2026-10-20

values.note: 'Little Fort is a first-come-first-serve minimally developed recreation area'; 'There are 9 sites available with no reservations required.'

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/little-fort-campground (OHV Camping Info: 'There are 9 sites available with no reservations required.'), read 2026-10-20

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/little-fort-campground ('Potable water is not available at this site.'; 'Restroom information is not available for this site.'), read 2026-10-20

summary: Confirmed no fee, first-come with no reservations (booking was derived from the note, now from USFS), and year-round season with the site open. Added 9 sites and no potable water. Not stated: restrooms ('information is not available'), hookups, site lengths.
flags: Possible off-road-scope question (curation doc: agency campgrounds that stage riders, 'a trailhead camp inside an OHV system', are out of scope): USFS lists Little Fort's camping under 'OHV Camping' and describes it as giving 'easy access right from the campground to the Peters Mill Run/Taskers Gap OHV trail system', 'the largest OHV system in the state of Virginia'. It is not named OHV and is not in audit/offroad_scope/decisions.jsonl. AWH added it (--AWH note), so a human should decide whether it is a general campground with an OHV side.
